newsitem.title: USA: Special counsel urged to probe Clinton witnesses.
newsitem.headline: Special counsel urged to probe Clinton witnesses.

text.p: A Republican House chairman Tuesday urged Independent Counsel Kenneth Starr to investigate possible misconduct by witnesses in hearings about the White House Travel Office firings and the handling of FBI files.

William Clinger, a Pennsylvania Republican, said Starr should look into whether witnesses with Clinton administration ties were guilty of perjury or obstruction of justice at House Government Reform Committee hearings Clinger chaired.

Clinger sent Starr copies of the committee's investigations of the firing of seven White House travel office employees in 1993 and improper requests by the White House personnel security office for several hundred FBI background files on leading Republicans.

Starr is investigating the involvement of President Bill Clinton and his wife Hillary in the Whitewater land development deal in Arkansas a decade ago and the failure of the Madison Savings and Loan Association.

"Our analysis of the documentary evidence and sworn statements suggests a significant degree of misconduct, as well as misleading and contradictory statements, that needs to be examined by the independent counsel," Clinger said in a statement. He said his committee had no authority to determine criminal violations.

"In particular, I have highlighted for the independent counsel's attention some of the testimony of Jane Sherburne, Harry Thomason, Craig Livingstone, Anthony Marceca, William Kennedy, Bernard Nussbaum and Thomas 'Mack' McLarty," he said.

Livingstone was in charge of the White House personnel security office and Marceca worked for him. McLarty was White House chief of staff in the first half of Clinton's term and is now a counsellor. Nussbaum was White House counsel and Kennedy was a White House aide. Sherburne is a White House aide and Thomason is a friend of the Clintons.
